cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: fictional copy for an invented AI product; two items noted as on file)
AAJ - CLAIMS & PROOF CHECK (audience: ai)
9 sentences: 5 need proof, 1 need consent, 1 to review wording, 2 with nothing flagged.
10 flags, 8 open, 2 with evidence noted as on file.
This flags claims that need support. It is not legal advice: check the legal consequences with counsel before publishing.
[1] NEEDS PROOF  "Meet Quillo, the AI-powered proposal writer for agencies."
proof    AI capability or accuracy claim: "AI-powered"   (s1-ai)

why:  Claims about what an AI product does, how accurate it is, or that it replaces people are ordinary advertising claims: they need evidence that the product performs as claimed, under the conditions a buyer will use it.

keep: The test behind each figure: data set, task, sample size, date, model version, and who ran it. For "AI-powered", a plain record of which feature uses which model. For "replaces", a side-by-side test against the people it is said to replace.

see:  FTC - Order Requires Workado to Back Up Artificial Intelligence Detection Claims (Apr 2025) - https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/04/ftc-order-requires-workado-back-artificial-intelligence-detection-claims
see:  FTC Announces Crackdown on Deceptive AI Claims and Schemes (Sep 2024) - https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/09/ftc-announces-crackdown-deceptive-ai-claims-schemes
see:  FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation
[2] NEEDS PROOF  "Quillo is 99% accurate and replaces your entire proposal team."
proof    AI capability or accuracy claim: "99% accurate · replaces your entire proposal team"   (s2-ai)

why:  Claims about what an AI product does, how accurate it is, or that it replaces people are ordinary advertising claims: they need evidence that the product performs as claimed, under the conditions a buyer will use it.

keep: The test behind each figure: data set, task, sample size, date, model version, and who ran it. For "AI-powered", a plain record of which feature uses which model. For "replaces", a side-by-side test against the people it is said to replace.

see:  FTC - Order Requires Workado to Back Up Artificial Intelligence Detection Claims (Apr 2025) - https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/04/ftc-order-requires-workado-back-artificial-intelligence-detection-claims
see:  FTC Announces Crackdown on Deceptive AI Claims and Schemes (Sep 2024) - https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/09/ftc-announces-crackdown-deceptive-ai-claims-schemes
see:  FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation
[3] NEEDS PROOF  "Teams using Quillo win 3x more deals and cut proposal time in half."
proof    Result or outcome claim: "more deals · cut proposal time"   (s3-outcome)

why:  A promise of a result (more revenue, better scores, less churn) is the claim a buyer is paying for. It needs evidence that the product causes it for buyers like them, not only for your best customer.
keep: The data behind the result: which customers, how many, over what period, measured how, and what else changed at the time. If it is one customer's result, say so in the copy.
see:  FTC - Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business
see:  FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation
proof    Specific number, percentage or multiplier: "3x"   (s3-number)
why:  A specific figure reads as measured fact. It needs the measurement behind it, and the copy should say what it is a figure of.
keep: The calculation and its inputs: the data source, the sample, the period, the baseline, and the date the figure was last checked.
see:  FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation
see:  FTC - Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business
[4] NEEDS PROOF  "Unlike Loopdeck, every draft is checked against your past wins."
proof    Comparison with a competitor or alternative: "Unlike Loopdeck"   (s4-comparative)
why:  Naming or implying a competitor invites the buyer, and the competitor, to check. A comparison is held to the same standard as any other claim: true, current and supported. Named here: Loopdeck.
keep: The side-by-side behind the comparison: what was compared, on which version and plan, the source for the competitor facts, and the date it was last checked.
see:  FTC Statement of Policy Regarding Comparative Advertising - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/statement-policy-regarding-comparative-advertising
see:  FTC - Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business
[5] NEEDS CONSENT  ""Quillo paid for itself in the first month." - Dana R., Head of Growth"
consent  Testimonial, endorsement or influencer: ""Quillo paid for itself in the first month.""   (s5-endorsement)

why:  A testimonial, a named customer, a logo or a creator post speaks for someone else. It must reflect their honest experience, you need their permission to use it, and any payment or other connection must be disclosed.

keep: Written permission from the person or company (what may be used, where, until when), the original words, any payment, free product or relationship to disclose, and evidence that the result they describe is what buyers can generally expect - or a clear statement of what is typical.
see:  FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking
[6] OK - EVIDENCE NOTED  "Rated 4.9 out of 5 from 1,200 reviews."
on file  Rating or review claim: "Rated 4.9 out of 5 · 1,200 reviews"   (s6-reviews)
evidence: s6-reviews
[7] NEEDS PROOF  "SOC 2 Type II certified, with bank-grade encryption."
on file  Compliance badge or certification: "SOC 2 Type II · certified"   (s7-compliance)
evidence: SOC 2 Type II: report dated 2026-06-30, covers production
proof    Security or privacy promise: "bank-grade encryption"   (s7-security)
why:  Security and privacy statements are product claims. If the safeguard is not in place, or the data is shared after all, the statement is what a buyer and a regulator will hold you to.

keep: The control behind each promise (encryption at rest and in transit, access controls, data-sharing list, retention policy), who verified it and when, and the privacy policy text that matches the copy.
see:  FTC - Start with Security: A Guide for Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/start-security-guide-business
[8] REVIEW WORDING  "Start your free trial today - no credit card required."
wording  "Free", "risk-free" or limited-time offer: "free · no credit card"   (s8-offer)
why:  An offer is judged by what the buyer has to do to get it. Conditions, renewal terms and real deadlines belong next to the offer, not in the small print.
keep: The full terms as published (what is free, for how long, what happens at the end, any card or purchase required), and for a deadline or "only N left", the record that it is real.
see:  FTC - Guide Concerning Use of the Word "Free" and Similar Representations - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/rules/guide-concerning-use-word-free-similar-representations
see:  FTC - Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business
[9] OK - NOTHING FLAGGED  "Set up takes about an hour with your own templates."
This flags claims that need support. It is not legal advice: check the legal consequences with counsel before publishing.

keep: The report, certificate or attestation, its scope (which product, which entities), its date and who issued it. For HIPAA, the safeguards and the signed business associate agreements; for FERPA and COPPA, the school agreements and data practices the claim rests on. The current report or certificate, its period and scope.

[4] REVIEW WORDING  "The only accounting platform built for multi-entity startups."
wording  Absolute or guarantee: "The only accounting platform"   (s4-absolute)
why:  "Only", "guaranteed", "100%", "never" or "zero" can be disproved by a single counterexample. If it is not literally true every time, the wording overclaims.
keep: Either evidence that it holds every time (and the written terms, for a guarantee), or a narrower wording that says what you do and how you know.
see:  FTC - Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business - https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business
see:  FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation - https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/ftc-policy-statement-regarding-advertising-substantiation
